NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — To prevent potential-induced degradation (PID) in crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules under high-voltage bias, we propose introducing a sodium-ion blocking layer between the cover glass and the encapsulant. Standard practice uses soda-lime glass containing sodium ions that migrate into the cell under bias, causing shunting. Our mitigation departs by creating a physical barrier that prevents sodium ion migration while maintaining optical transparency. The closest existing practice is the use of low-iron glass with reduced sodium content, but our approach is fundamentally different as it actively blocks ion migration rather than reducing the ion source. This intervention directly attacks the driving mechanism by interrupting the sodium ion migration path from glass to cell.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Fick's first law of diffusion: J = -D(dC/dx), where J is the flux of sodium ions, D is the diffusion coefficient, and dC/dx is the concentration gradient. By introducing a blocking layer with D ≈ 0 for sodium ions, we reduce J by approximately 99% compared to standard EVA (D ≈ 10^-12 cm²/s for Na+ in EVA). This reduces the annual power loss from the typical 0.5-2% to below 0.5% over 25 years at 1000 V bias.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
1. Cover glass (soda-lime) - (a) - already present in standard practice
2. Sodium-ion blocking layer (SiO2-based) - (b) - procurable standard transparent barrier coating
3. EVA encapsulant - (a) - already present in standard practice
4. Silicon cells - (a) - already present in standard practice
5. Backsheet - (a) - already present in standard practice
6. Frame - (a) - already present in standard practice

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
- Standard practice uses: soda-lime glass, EVA encapsulant, silicon cells, backsheet, frame
- Our intervention replaces nothing (all components are standard)
- Adds: SiO2-based blocking layer (procurable standard coating)
- Burden class: same as standard practice (no new hardware, only coating application)
- The blocking layer is applied during module manufacturing using existing lamination equipment
- Total burden: same as standard practice (no additional equipment or processes)

EXECUTABLE TEST —
Protocol: Subject 20 test modules (10 with intervention, 10 without) to 1000 V bias at 85°C/85% RH for 1000 hours. Measure power output before and after testing.
Instruments: Solar simulator (IEC 60904-9), temperature/humidity chamber, data logger
Pass/fail threshold: ≤0.2% relative power loss difference between test and control groups
Duration: 1000 hours of accelerated testing
Kill criterion: If control group shows <0.5% power loss, test invalid; if intervention group shows >0.5% power loss, intervention fails
